column15: No web presence found this session; own-label, origin unclear despite the IE country guess from the catalogue.

No web presence found; own-label, could not confirm this is genuine whisky vs. another Spanish spirit category. Catalogue guesses blend/ES; kept (unlike 'Haran', see report) since nothing here explicitly signals a non-whisky oak-chip product.

Organic-certified Scotch whisky brand; recalled to be French-marketed but official sites (highlandharvest.se/.fr) did not resolve this session, so ownership and peat character could not be confirmed by citation. Source distillery undisclosed. Left peat unknown per policy rather than rely on memory.

Catalogue's own product name states the producer directly ("House of Maclair Ian Macleod"). Ian Macleod Distillers is confirmed real (Wikipedia), but this specific range is not among the brands the article lists (Isle of Skye, Sheep Dip, Pig's Nose, King Robert II, etc.), so peat is left unknown rather than inherit the parent company's other house styles.
No citable source found this session for this Irish whiskey despite the name being familiar; left unknown rather than rely on memory.

Loch Lomond distillery's own-named single malt brand (12 Year Old etc., per Wikipedia's product list). Whisky literature widely describes Inchmurrin as the unpeated/fruity style contrasted with peated sibling Inchmoan, but three fetches this session (Wikipedia raw text, lochlomondgroup.com, a scotchwhisky.com attempt) found no explicit peat statement, so left unknown rather than assert from memory. REVIEWER FLAG: likely 'none' if independently confirmed -- do not average with Inchmoan/Croftengea (heavily peated siblings, not in this batch).
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row. This gap's catalogue supplied no type/country for this product; corrected to GB-SCT/blend since this is a well-documented Ian Macleod Distillers brand.
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts): Lincoln County Process charcoal mellowing removes impurities rather than adding smoke, so no peat/smoky claim.

Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). "John Walker & Sons" (this batch's Blue/Red/Gold-Centenary/XR cluster) is Diageo's premium packaging of the same Johnnie Walker family, not a separate house style -- handled via alias below rather than a new producer row.
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts): pure/vatted malt blended from Scottish and Japanese malt whisky; no peat information found for the sourced components.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy for one-product long-tail brands.
Redwood Empire's "Lost Monarch Small Batch Craft Whiskey Blend" (confirmed via their own site) -- a blend of bourbon and rye. Standard American whiskey, no peat mentioned.

Northern California craft whiskey producer. Range spans bourbon, rye, blend and a single malt ("Foggy Burl"), so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere in the lineup; standard American whiskey.
Redwood Empire's "Pipe Dream Bourbon Whiskey" (confirmed via their own site). Standard American whiskey, no peat.

Could not confirm this session (domain lookups failed, no Wikipedia page). Unconfirmed personal recollection that this may be a French independent bottler of sourced (non-French) malt whisky rather than a French distillery -- flagged for human review rather than acted on without a citation.
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess at all; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear.

Copper Rivet Distillery's whisky brand (Chatham, Kent) -- confirmed via Wikipedia's list of English whisky distilleries ("Copper Rivet Distillery ... set to launch Masthouse whisky"). defaultTypeName left empty: this batch's own product name says "Column Distilled" (implying a continuous/grain still) while Wikipedia describes the first release as single malt, suggesting the range spans more than one type. No peat statement found (copperrivetdistillery.com returned 403 both times fetched).
Added because Masthouse (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Chatham, Kent; also makes Dockyard gin and Vela vodka (not whisky).

Morris of Rutherglen -- Casella Family Brands has sold whisky under this legacy fortified-wine brand since 2021 (confirmed via Wikipedia), using Muscat/Port/Sherry/Tokay fortified-wine cask finishes (all named in this batch's samples). No peat/smoke statement found for the base range. This batch also has a "Morris Smoked Muscat Barrel" -- deliberately NOT given a rule.tsv row: 'smoked' could mean peat-smoke or a non-peat wood-smoke and no source distinguishes which, so guessing would risk exactly the wrong-row-is-worse-than-no-row failure. REVIEWER FLAG: check this specific release.

Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). This gap's catalogue spells it "Naked Malt" -- Edrington's own URL slug is literally /naked-malt/, confirming this is a real alternate/market-specific name for the same product, not a different brand.

Could not verify this brand this session (no Wikipedia page, no resolvable official site). Flagged for a human to check authenticity -- some Japanese-sounding export blends are not actually distilled in Japan.

Undisclosed-source single malt label per BRIEF.md's rule 3 (same pattern as "Secret Orkney"/"Speyside's Finest"), named after Edinburgh's historic (drained) Nor Loch. No web presence found this session; not guessing the source distillery.
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). This batch's sample: "Octomore 15.1 Scottish Barley Edition".

Added because Octomore and Port Charlotte (this batch) reference it via parentSlug. Core own-name range is unpeated; Port Charlotte (heavy) and Octomore (extreme) are separate sibling rows, never averaged in.

Two catalogue entries share this stem with different invented-sounding regional flourishes ("Highland Phantom Peak", "Speyside Celestia Creek"); no web presence found for either. Likely an own-label range with a region-themed name per bottling, but the specific distillery/region cannot be confirmed, so region is left empty rather than picked arbitrarily; kept as one producer row covering both catalogue entries.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.

No web presence found. Catalogue calls it "bourbon" but it is sold from Spain, an unusual combination -- left type/peat unknown rather than trust the bourbon guess. Similar unidentifiable own-label pattern to the existing "Jim Bardett" row from another batch (different spelling; not assumed to be the same producer).
Historic low-priced Kentucky straight bourbon brand, distilled by Suntory Global Spirits (Beam Suntory) alongside Jim Beam (confirmed via Wikipedia search result text). Standard bourbon, no peat.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear -- possibly an invented Irish-sounding name rather than genuinely Irish.

Diageo's rare/sourced-whiskey project releasing single malts and bourbons from various (including mothballed) distilleries under many release names (Rhetoric, Barterhouse, Old Blowhard, Muckety-Muck, Woven Honor...). Bottler-style range, no single house peat level.

Rhetoric is an aged-bourbon release under the Orphan Barrel project; the specific source distillery/mashbill for this release was not confirmed this session so kept as kind=blend rather than naming a distillery. Standard bourbon category, no peat.

Originally created by Spencerfield Spirit Company; acquired by Ian Macleod Distillers with their purchase of Spencerfield Spirits in September 2016 (confirmed via Wikipedia). Listed among Ian Macleod's core blended-Scotch brands, explicitly contrasted there with their peated Smokehead single malt -- read as implicitly unpeated.

Jacopo Poli is a well-known Italian grappa/brandy house (Bassano del Grappa, Veneto); could not confirm this session whether "Segretario di Stato" is genuinely a whisky release of theirs or a mislabeled grappa/brandy product (poligrappa.com returned 404 / redirected to an Italian-only page with no whisky content found). Kept as a low/unknown-confidence row rather than skipped outright, since the catalogue explicitly classifies it "malt"/IT -- flagged for human review of whether this is whisky at all.

No web presence found (no Wikipedia page, no resolvable official site) despite three samples in this batch (Bourbon Casks, Peated Small Batch No.2, Selected Casks) suggesting a small/single-cask-style range. See rule.tsv for the "Peated" exception, evidenced directly by the product's own name rather than an external source.
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear.

Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts): Highland distillery, owned by John Dewar & Sons (Bacardi); confirmed against this project's own local Wikipedia distillery reference file (region=Highland).
No web presence found; own-label, origin unclear. Catalogue's own country guess was blank.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.

No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy. Catalogue has two near-duplicate rows for this name (one typed "blend", one untyped) -- both covered by the one alias below.

Own site (fetched) confirms "Product of Scotland" / blended Scotch with a range of Finest, Smoky, Beer Reserve and Aged 12 Years. "Finest" (this batch's product, catalogued as "Sir Edwards Finests", a typo) is the base unpeated blend; see rule.tsv for the separately-named "Smoky" variant. Owner recorded from this project's brief-provided background (French-owned via La Martiniquaise) -- not independently re-confirmed by a fetched source this session (the homepage did not state an owner), so treat that one fact with some caution.

No web presence found. Possibly a French-market fake-Scottish-sounding brand in the same naming pattern as Sir Edward's ("Sir X"), but unconfirmed this session -- not assumed to be the same producer/owner.

Small distillery near Kingussie (Tromie Mills), producing SPEY and Beinn Dubh single malts under the Speyside Distillery name (confirmed via Wikipedia); mothballed 2025 per the fetched article, which does not affect whisky already distilled/bottled such as this batch's 1991 vintage sample. No peat statement found in the article; "none" follows the general Highland/Speyside malt convention rather than a distillery-specific statement. Also cross-checked against this project's local Wikipedia distillery reference file, which independently lists it as Speyside region (closed).

Owner stated directly by the catalogue's own product name ("The Forge Hibernia Distillers"); hiberniadistillers.com resolves (real domain) but is currently just a "coming soon" placeholder with no product content, so range/peat details could not be confirmed.

Linlithgow, Lowland distillery, closed 1983 (Diageo is the corporate successor of DCL; the physical site is now flats). No peat statement found in the fetched article, left unknown rather than assume the general Lowland-style convention. This batch's sample references an "Authentic Collection" bottler range, which could not be independently confirmed this session (Wikipedia's Duncan Taylor page is a bare disambiguation stub), so no bottlerSlug is set.

Nikka's "Pure Malt" vatting of Yoichi and Miyagikyo malt whiskies (named for founder Masataka Taketsuru), owned by Asahi Group Holdings via Nikka. Yoichi is widely understood to contribute a peated component but the fetched Wikipedia article states no peat/smoke detail and whisky.com returned 403, so left unknown rather than assert a level from memory. REVIEWER FLAG: likely 'light' if independently confirmed -- matches this project's existing 'nikka' row's identical flag for Yoichi.

Catalogue supplied no type/country guess at all (unusual -- even the shop could not classify it), and no web presence found this session. Flagged for human review of authenticity; "Takumi" (Japanese for 'artisan/craftsman') is also a generic marketing word used by unrelated brands, which is why its alias below is scope=brand rather than any.

Reused slug from an earlier batch. Own site (fetched) confirms Templeton now distills its own whiskey in Templeton, Iowa, and makes bourbon ("Fortitude", a high-rye bourbon, this batch's product) as well as rye -- range spans types so defaultTypeName is left empty and kind is corrected to distillery. Standard American whiskey, no peat.
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). "The Grouse & Cola" (this batch) is a ready-mixed RTD of the same blend with cola -- handled via alias below rather than a separate producer row.
Confirmed via Douglas Laing's own site as part of their "Specialist Selection" blended range; no tasting notes/peat statement found there.
Added because King of Scots (this batch) references it via bottlerSlug. Independent bottler est. 1948, Glasgow.

Own site (fetched) confirms production at Boann Distillery, Co. Meath, by Prestige Beverage Group; range spans blend and single malt lines (Double Oaked, Trilogy, Cask Finish series, plus a dedicated Single Malt line) so defaultTypeName is left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned in the fetched range description; standard Irish whiskey.

Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). "Tottori Barell" (this batch, likely a typo for "Barrel") is treated as the same brand family via the shared "Tottori" alias rather than a separate row -- its catalogue type guess of "bourbon" is probably a cask-finish descriptor, not a literal bourbon whiskey.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.

Named for the Irish revolutionary; catalogue has both a "single malt" (Beara) and a "blend" (Rich Blend Beara) variant of this brand, so defaultTypeName is left empty and kind is kept as blend (undisclosed single distillery of origin) rather than asserting one. No web presence found this session; "Beara" suggests a West Cork-area connection but this is unconfirmed, so no owner/parentSlug is guessed.
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). This gap's catalogue spells it in Cyrillic ("Глен Таллок", transliterating as "Glen Tallok") -- see Cyrillic alias below.

Own site (fetched) confirms "American Single Malt" whisky, self-described as "the most awarded single malt whisky distillery in America"; no explicit peat/smoke statement found, but no peated expression is known in their range either -- standard unpeated American single malt. This batch's sample is a Port Cask finish.
Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts). This batch's sample: "Port Charlotte Islay Barley Bruichladdich".

Added because Inchmurrin (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Reused slug from an earlier batch's row (same facts): the eponymous Loch Lomond spirit is unpeated; the distillery also makes heavily peated siblings under other names (Inchmoan, Croftengea, not in this batch).
